# `Browser.Push.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Push.Internals — the low-level push subscription port surface:
the opaque application key and subscription, their one parser and one encoder,
and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` request wiring the high-level
`Ipe.Browser.Push` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:push` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.Push` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

The outbound command type is private: the only way to ask the host for a
subscription is `requestSubscribe` with an `ApplicationKey`, so a key that
failed `applicationKey` has no representation on the port.

## `ApplicationKey`

An application server's public key: a 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point,
held as its canonical unpadded base64url text. The only constructor is
`applicationKey`.

## `Subscription`

A push subscription the host returned, one variant per transport. The only
constructor is `decodeSubscription`; `encodeSubscription` is its one
canonical rendering.

## `applicationKey`

```ipe
applicationKey : String -> Result Error ApplicationKey
```

`applicationKey text` — parse an application server's public key.

`Ok` only for exactly 87 characters of unpadded base64url, in their one
canonical spelling, that decode to 65 bytes starting with the uncompressed
point tag `0x04`. Anything else is an `Error.invalidInput`.

## `decodeSubscription`

```ipe
decodeSubscription : String -> Result Error Subscription
```

`decodeSubscription text` — parse a canonical subscription text.

`Ok` only for a text within the byte ceiling whose version, kind and fields
each parse, and which is exactly the text `encodeSubscription` renders for the
result: a second spelling of the same subscription is refused.

## `encodeSubscription`

```ipe
encodeSubscription : Subscription -> String
```

`encodeSubscription subscription` — the one canonical subscription text.

Its string escapes are `Ipe.Json.Encode`'s, which also escape `<`, `>`, `&`,
U+2028 and U+2029, so a host that renders the text must spell them the same
way or `decodeSubscription` refuses it.

## `requestSubscribe`

```ipe
requestSubscribe : ApplicationKey -> Task Error Subscription
```

`requestSubscribe key` — ask the host to subscribe this device under `key`.

## `requestCurrent`

```ipe
requestCurrent : Task Error (Maybe Subscription)
```

`requestCurrent` — ask the host for this device's current subscription.

## `requestUnsubscribe`

```ipe
requestUnsubscribe : Task Error ()
```

`requestUnsubscribe` — ask the host to drop this device's subscription.

## `subscribeReply`

```ipe
subscribeReply : Decode.Decoder (Result Error Subscription)
```

The reply to a subscribe request: a `subscribed` event carrying a
subscription text that `decodeSubscription` accepts, or a refusal.

## `currentReply`

```ipe
currentReply : Decode.Decoder (Result Error (Maybe Subscription))
```

The reply to a current request: a `current` event carrying a subscription
text or `null`, or a refusal.

## `unsubscribeReply`

```ipe
unsubscribeReply : Decode.Decoder (Result Error ())
```

The reply to an unsubscribe request: an `unsubscribed` event, or a refusal.
